about.title: Temple City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Temple City sees a steady flow of traffic moving between Rosemead Boulevard, Lower Azusa Road, and the Las Tunas Drive corridor, and public records show 93 injury collisions in the most recent year, with 111 people hurt and 3 lives lost. Thursday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. tend to see the most reported crashes, likely tied to end-of-week commute and school pickup traffic converging near local intersections. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter: photos of the scene, witness names, and medical records can disappear or fade quickly. LawProactive is a free service — not a law firm — that connects injured Temple City residents with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with Los Angeles County claims. There's no cost to talk with someone, and no fee unless your case results in a recovery. You don't have to sort through insurance calls and paperwork by yourself while you're trying to heal.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Most When Building a Car Accident Claim

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim in California, but if a government entity — like the city or a public agency — was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting early keeps your options open.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage you're found responsible. What you say to the other driver's insurer, especially in a recorded statement, can be used to shift blame onto you — it's worth having guidance before you speak with them.

items.title: No Cap, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

items.question: I was in a crash near Lower Azusa Road and the insurance adjuster wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: It's generally wise to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can minimize your claim or shift fault onto you under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Temple City?
items.answer: California's standard statute of limitations is two years from the date of the crash, but if a government entity or public roadway defect was involved, you may have as little as six months to act. Because Temple City's streets include intersections maintained by different agencies, it's worth having a claim evaluated promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so you may still recover compensation even if you share some blame — your award is simply reduced by your percentage of fault. This is one reason preserving evidence early, before memories fade or footage is deleted, matters so much.

items.question: Is there really no cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct — LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if your case results in a recovery.
